name: refactor_sql_subquery_to_join
description: Refactors a correlated subquery into a LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY producing the identical result set
prompts: query.sql lists every customer with the number of orders they have placed, using a correlated subquery in the SELECT list: (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id). Refactor it to compute order_count with a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders plus GROUP BY, removing the correlated subquery. The result set must be identical: one row per customer ordered by c.id, with order_count = number of their orders, and a customer with zero orders must still appear with order_count 0. Return columns id, name, order_count in that order.

setup_files.query.sql:
-- For every customer, the number of orders they have placed (0 if none).
SELECT c.id, c.name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
ORDER BY c.id;

reference_solution.query.sql:
-- For every customer, the number of orders they have placed (0 if none).
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;

files.query.sql:
-- DRIFT: INNER JOIN drops customers who have no orders.
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;
